headline: South Korea's financial authorities have postponed choosing firms for the second round of relaxed network-separation rules because of the wave of hacks on banks.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a concrete regulatory consequence dated 6 Oct; the report is a secondary account of Korean sources.
importance_line: Bank customers and the roughly 500 financial firms now doing emergency self-inspections are affected, and the hacks have delayed a plan to let firms use outside AI tools to find weaknesses in their own systems, but authorities say they will not reverse the overall policy and the report is a secondary account that does not name its original source.
source: BigGo Finance, citing South Korean financial authorities
summary: BigGo Finance, citing South Korean financial authorities, reports that on 6 Oct 2026 the Financial Services Commission postponed choosing firms for the second round of an easing of network-separation rules, which limit financial firms' use of outside AI and security services, because of the hacking wave across the sector; the selection had been due on 7 Oct. This continues the story we carried on 5 Oct 2026 about seven financial companies hit by attacks; the new development is the postponement, and the article adds that first-round participants Shinhan Bank and Hana Bank were among those breached and quotes a Financial Security Institute official saying AI was used, but only as a tool by a human hacker, not acting on its own.
notes: Read in full. Aggregator article; the original Korean outlet is not named and no English original was found. Only the postponement is certainly new today. Same story line as C12-01 and C12-09.
